changes.old: ### GradCache: full-batch negatives with chunked encoder passes With two training pairs, let both the query and document inputs be the rows
changes.new: ### GradCache: full-batch negatives with chunked encoder passes Split four query–document pairs into two chunks, pairs 1–2 and 3–4. In the figure, rows are queries and columns are documents. A query's positive is on the diagonal; the other documents in its row are negatives if the labels say they are irrelevant. ![[00 Учебник/Assets/Figures/curated/gradcache-comparison-2026-11-09/contaccum-figure1.png|Three panels: GradCache uses all 16 query–document scores; gradient accumulation uses only the two 2-by-2 diagonal blocks; ContAccum mixes current and detached past representations]] *Jaehee Kim, Yukyung Lee, Pilsung Kang, [A Gradient Accumulation Method for Dense Retriever under Memory Constraint, Figure 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.12356v3#S2.F1). [Original PNG](https://arxiv.org/html/2406.12356v3/Styles/figures/comparison-camera_ready.png), unchanged, [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).* In **(a)** GradCache computes the row loss over all four columns. Query 1 has three negatives, including documents 3 and 4 in the other chunk. In **(b)** ordinary gradient accumulation computes each loss separately, over just two columns. Query 1 has only document 2 as a negative. The empty blocks in (b) are absent from the softmax; they are not zero-valued logits. For the score row $(1,0,0,0)$, the loss for query 1 is $\log(1+3/e)\approx0.7437$ in (a) and $\log(1+1/e)\approx0.3133$ in (b). Accumulating the weight gradients cannot put the two missing terms back into the denominator. In **(c)** [[05 Источники/Papers/ContAccum|ContAccum]] appends four saved query vectors and four saved document vectors to the two current pairs. A current query now compares its positive with five negatives. A saved document affects the gradient of the current query but receives no gradient through its old encoder pass; the hatched cells show comparisons with one trainable side. This changes the loss. GradCache instead recomputes encoder activations for the same examples and preserves the full-batch objective. With two training pairs, let both the query and document inputs be the rows

sources: Gao et al. RepL4NLP 2021 §§3.1–3.4 and pinned GradCache source 906f0383: full-batch objective, representation derivatives and recomputation conditions.
Kim, Lee and Kang arXiv v3 §§2.1, 3.1–3.3 and Figure 1. CC BY 4.0 applies to this version. The figure is the complete author PNG, 5140×2010, unchanged.
review.examples: The figure's four current pairs give 3 negatives per query in GradCache and 1 with isolated microbatch loss. For scores (1,0,0,0), the losses are log(1+3/e) and log(1+1/e). The six-pair memory-bank check keeps old vectors detached but checks that they influence current gradients. The old two-pair GradCache example and full method excerpt remain.
